assertions.text: Table has at least one column name ending with '?' (e.g. 'Discount?' or 'Expected?')
Table has exactly 3 data rows (GOLD, SILVER, BRONZE)
assertions.evidence: Gold customer | GOLD..., Silver customer | SILVER..., Bronze customer | BRONZE...

assertions.text: Test method body contains only one assertEquals (or equivalent assertion) — not three
Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: Method body contains only single assertEquals call, no conditionals

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: Scenario | tier | amount | Discount? (Scenario is leftmost)

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case
assertions.evidence: void calculatesDiscountByTier(...) reads as 'Calculates Discount By Tier'

assertions.text: If @Description is present, it provides context beyond what the table rows already express. It is acceptable to omit @Description if the table already conveys all relevant context.
assertions.evidence: @Description is absent; table fully conveys context (acceptable per rule)

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Only @TableTest present; no violations of annotation order

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string). Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description is absent, so assertion passes per rule
